question.english: People go to banks for various reasons. Tell me about what you typically do when you visit a bank, and describe how banking services have changed compared to the past.
question.korean: 사람들은 다양한 이유로 은행에 갑니다. 보통 은행에 갈 때 어떤 업무를 보시는지, 그리고 과거와 비교해 은행 서비스가 어떻게 변했는지 말씀해 주세요.
question.combo_context: 돌발주제 '은행' 3단 콤보 중 첫 번째 문항으로, 평소 은행 업무 루틴과 과거 대비 변화상을 함께 묻는 비교/묘사 복합형 질문입니다.

model_answer.script:
Honestly, looking back, visiting a physical bank branch used to be a real chore. In the past, whenever I had to open a bank account or apply for a loan, I had to wait in line forever. But nowadays, banking has changed drastically thanks to mobile banking apps.

The thing is, I rarely visit brick-and-mortar branches anymore because I can handle financial transactions right on my smartphone. With just a few taps, I can transfer funds between accounts or manage my savings account in seconds. It has truly simplified daily life. On top of that, mobile apps make it so easy to track spending habits in real time, which helps me stay on budget without carrying physical cash around.

That being said, when it comes to complex tasks like dealing with an unexpected account freeze, I still visit a physical branch. The teller greeted me warmly and helped me resolve the issue swiftly, saving me from a potential financial headache.

All in all, while mobile banking handles 90 percent of my routine tasks, having professional tellers ready for urgent matters gives me great peace of mind.
model_answer.structure_note: 서론(과거 은행 방문의 번거로움과 현재 모바일 뱅킹으로의 전환) → MP(모바일 앱을 통한 금융 거래 및 지출 관리의 편리함) → 디테일 확장(계좌 동결 등 복잡한 문제 시 오프라인 지점 방문 경험) → 감정/생각(기술 편의성과 대면 지원의 안도감) → 마무리(디지털과 대면 서비스의 조화 요약)
al_points: 'visiting a physical bank branch used to be... But nowadays...' 구조를 사용해 과거의 불편함과 현재의 편리함을 극명하게 대비했습니다.
'financial transactions', 'track spending habits', 'account freeze'와 같은 금융 주제 핵심 콜로케이션을 자연스럽게 구사했습니다.
'The thing is', 'That being said', 'All in all' 등 담화 표지어를 적재적소에 배치해 답변의 논리적 흐름과 유창성을 크게 높였습니다.

patterns.pattern: Whenever I had to [verb], I had to [verb] forever.
patterns.meaning: ~해야 할 때마다, 한참 동안/끝도 없이 ~해야만 했습니다.
patterns.usage_today: In the past, whenever I had to open a bank account or apply for a loan, I had to wait in line forever.
patterns.extra_example: In the past, whenever I had to renew my passport, I had to wait in line forever at the embassy.

patterns.pattern: When it comes to [complex task/issue], I still [action].
patterns.meaning: ~와 같은 복잡한 일/문제에 관해서는, 저는 여전히 ~합니다.
patterns.usage_today: That being said, when it comes to complex tasks like dealing with an unexpected account freeze, I still visit a physical branch.
patterns.extra_example: When it comes to major life decisions like buying a home, I still consult with my parents.

checklist: 오늘 단어(open a bank account, transfer funds 등)를 4개 이상 자연스럽게 썼는가?
과거(used to, had to wait)와 현재(can handle, make it easy) 시제 대조가 흔들리지 않았는가?
MP(모바일 뱅킹 편리함) 후 구체적인 디테일(송금, 오프라인 방문 사례)을 2개 이상 확장했는가?
금융 업무 처리 후 느낀 안도감이나 생각(peace of mind)을 진솔하게 표현했는가?
전체 답변을 깔끔하게 요약하는 마무리 문장(All in all...)을 완성했는가?
필러(you know, the thing is)를 활용하여 3초 이상의 어색한 침묵 없이 유창하게 말했는가?
